subject: stamp-op-time
body:
## Description

R1: Every `create` operation the store accepts records `applied_at`, a UTC ISO-8601 time with a `+00:00` offset.
R2: Every `write` operation the store accepts (update, supersede, correct) records `applied_at`.
R3: Every `delete` operation the store accepts records `applied_at`.
R7: Opening a store with operations that have no time leaves every stored operation unchanged.

## Approach

In `orchestra/canon/sqlite_backend.py` add a module helper that returns `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="microseconds")` and put its result under `applied_at` in the op dict built in `SqliteBackend._write` and `SqliteBackend.delete_record`. Add `applied_at: JsonValue` to `_OptionalOp` in `orchestra/canon/types.py`. Change nothing else: not `fold`, not the schema, not `import_op`.

Write `tests/canon/test_op_time.py`. Build a temporary store with the `project` fixture from `tests/canon/conftest.py` and read ops with `open_backend(project.store_path).iter_chains()`. Name tests `test_r1_<behavior>`, `test_r2_<behavior>` (one for update, one for supersede or correct), `test_r3_<behavior>` (call `backend.delete_record`) and `test_r7_<behavior>`. For R7, insert op rows without `applied_at` straight into a fresh `ops` table with `sqlite3`, open the project, run `records()`, `get` and `validate()`, then compare `SELECT * FROM ops` before and after. Assert each time parses with `datetime.fromisoformat`, has a zero UTC offset, and lies between two `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` readings taken around the call. Run the R1 to R3 tests first and see them fail on the missing key.
title: Stamp a time on each new store operation

subject: pin-time-flows
body:
## Description

R8: `canon export` then `canon import` into an empty store keeps each operation's `applied_at` value, or its absence.

## Approach

Add `tests/canon/test_op_time_flow.py`. `test_r8_<behavior>`: create and update a record, add a legacy op row without a time to a second record, run `export_ops` from `orchestra/canon/transfer.py` into a `StringIO`, run `import_ops` into a fresh `SqliteBackend`, then compare `iter_chains()` of both stores op by op. No production code changes; `transfer.py` copies op keys as they are. Also write `test_r9_<behavior>` here: with the `cli` and `project` fixtures run `canon create` then `canon update --transition` through the CLI, then assert `project.history(id)` has strictly increasing `applied_at` values and the matching states. The R9 acceptance sits on the verification task.
title: Pin the time through export, import and the CLI

subject: verify-operation-timestamps
body:
## Description

Prove the phase exit criteria hold together: run the CLI flow check through the real entry point, then the canon test tree and the type and lint gates.

## Approach

R9: A record created, then updated through the `canon` CLI shows increasing times in its history.
R10: The existing canon tests pass.
R11: The change is clean under basedpyright, ruff check, ruff format.

Run the acceptance commands with `orchestra check` in the phase worktree `/home/andrewyin/orchestra/.worktrees/operation-timestamps`. Do not edit the tree. Return `fail` with the output if a check fails.
title: Verify operation timestamps

subject: read-op-history
body:
## Description

R4: `Project.history(record_id)` lists the accepted operations of the record, oldest first, as entries with the keys `seq`, `kind`, `lifecycle_state`, `revision`, `applied_at`.
R5: A history entry for an operation stored without `applied_at` reports `applied_at` as `None`.
R6: After a record moves to a new state, the history entry with that state carries a time within the span of the update call.

## Approach

Add `read_chain(self, record_id: str) -> list[StoredOp]` to the `Backend` protocol in `orchestra/canon/backend.py` and to `SqliteBackend` (open `_reader()` and return `_chain`). Add a `RecordChange` TypedDict to `orchestra/canon/types.py` with `seq: int`, `kind: str`, `lifecycle_state: str | None`, `revision: str | None`, `applied_at: str | None`. Add `Project.history(self, record_id: str) -> list[RecordChange]` in `orchestra/canon/project.py`: read the chain with `store.read_chain`, raise `StoreError` for an unknown id (empty chain), keep ops with `outcome == "accepted"`, and take `lifecycle_state` and `revision` from `op["record"]` (None for a delete op). `applied_at` is the op value when it is a string, else `None`. Docstring: say that the time a record entered a state is the `applied_at` of the first entry with that state.

Tests go in `tests/canon/test_op_time.py`, named `test_r4_<behavior>`, `test_r5_<behavior>` and `test_r6_<behavior>`. For R5 insert a legacy op row with `sqlite3` as in the `test_r7_` test. First add `history` as a stub that returns `[]`, run the tests and see them fail on the assertions, then implement.
title: Read a record's operation history with times

subject: read-op-history
verify_command: uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --confcutdir=tests/canon tests/canon/test_op_time.py -k "test_r4_ or test_r5_ or test_r6_"
